summary: The Load Forecasting Enhancement Act requires the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to establish regional joint boards to study electric load forecasting, identify best practices, and report recommendations to Congress. It modifies the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require state regulatory authorities to consider adopting these recommendations, and changes the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to make federal assistance for state energy conservation plans contingent upon including procedures to improve electric load forecasting accuracy, oversight, and transparency.

affected_groups.effect: Must establish regional joint boards, chair them, run them jointly with state commissions, and publish a report with best practices and recommendations for Congress.
Must participate in regional joint boards, and consider adopting the resulting electric load forecasting standards within specified timeframes.
Subject to state consideration of new electric load forecasting standards and requirements to improve forecasting accuracy, transparency, and stakeholder oversight.

key_provisions: Requires FERC to establish regional joint boards within 90 days of enactment, composed of state commission representatives and chaired by a FERC member, to study and identify best practices for electric load forecasting.
Directs FERC to publish and submit a report to Congress within one year detailing the identified best practices and recommendations for consistent use across states.
Requires state public utility commissions to commence consideration of the FERC-recommended load forecasting standard within one year and complete it within two years.

Modifies the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to require state energy conservation plans to include procedures and programs improving the accuracy, oversight, and transparency of electric load forecasting to receive federal assistance.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or authorizations allocated to FERC or states to carry out the studies and new planning requirements.
Specific penalties or definitions regarding the exact criteria for federal energy conservation plan assistance withdrawal beyond the statutory text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Load Forecasting Enhancement Act requires the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to establish regional joint boards to study electric load forecasting, identify best practices, and report recommendations to Congress. It modifies the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require state regulatory authorities to consider adopting these recommendations, and changes the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to make federal assistance for state energy conservation plans contingent upon including procedures to improve electric load forecasting accuracy, oversight, and transparency.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a structured federal-state framework to review and standardize how electricity demand is predicted across the United States. By linking federal energy conservation plan funding and state utility regulatory processes to forecasted load accuracy, the legislation aims to enhance the reliability and affordability of electric service nationwide.
